tools.name: board

scripts.name: board
scripts.cmd: node tools/board/stats.mjs && node tools/board/brand.mjs && node tools/board/cast.mjs && node tools/board/world.mjs && node tools/board/tools.mjs

tools.why: #178: what the build weighs, written where the board can read it. Measured from `dist/` after a build rather than typed anywhere, so it cannot disagree with the thing that shipped. `npm run board` after `npm run build`.

tools.name: checks
tools.why: #179: the runner. npm run check every free check, and every cheap one npm run check -- --free only the ones that need nothing but the source (milliseconds) npm run check -- --area Walls run one area npm run check -- --list what exists, what it costs, when it last ran npm run check -- --id walls-solid Results are written to `public/board/checks.json`, which is what the board's Tests page fetches. tools.name: imports
tools.why: Drop model files exported from other tools here (Meshy, Blockbench, Mixamo...).

tools.name: layout
tools.why: Birds-eye plan of the village with every pad bought, for eyeballing what check.mjs can only count. node tools/layout/plan.mjs settlement --tier 2 --span 42 It boots the built game headless, buys every pad it can reach, reveals all four roads, then swaps the camera for an overhead orthographic one and writes .shots/<name>.jpg. tools.name: models
tools.why: `tools/models/clips.mjs` writes the `Death` and `Hit` animation clips into the character GLBs.

tools.name: probe
tools.why: `?perf=1` shows you the numbers while you play. The probe collects the same numbers without you, so a change can be measured instead of argued about.

tools.name: scout
tools.why: The agents the scout runs. Each one is a separate headless Claude Code process with its own brief, its own tools, and a strict JSON answer. They are deliberately narrow: an agent asked for "improvements" returns mush, an agent asked "what does a new player misunderstand in the first three minutes, and what in this repository causes it" returns something you can act on. `tools` is passed to --allowed-tools. Keep it…

tools.name: triage
tools.why: #207: reads a new issue the moment it is opened and rewrites it as a ticket in this repo's own terms -- what is actually wrong, where it probably lives, how anyone would know it was done, and what it costs to do.
